## D-089 — 2026-10-04 PO note batch N64–N73 — 2026-10-05
- PO approved the Product directions for N64–N73 as classified in the active Product Ledger, with N64 explicitly last priority and N72 explicitly deferred to a dedicated later iPhone/Safari lane.
- N65/N66/N67 form an eligible low-risk micro-batch: collapse former-students history, remove redundant «كل الفصول» contextual link, and keep Desktop Mini Hub visible inside teaching routes. Each N-ID keeps separate acceptance/evidence; D-086 responsive coverage applies.
- N68 is approved as a presentation-gate fix only. Do not alter Sync scheduling/outbox semantics or suppress durable rejected/blocked/failed/Auth/ownership/data-risk conditions. Normal wake/reconnect recovery should remain quiet in Mini Hub until stable failure is proven.
- N69 is approved: attendance-report date range moves into the main toolbar as calm compact `من:` / `إلى:` controls; desktop may be one row, compact mobile may wrap naturally. Do not preserve the current bulky date-box treatment.
- N70 direction approved: Work must show three integrated Reports-page IA variants; PO selects before Freeze/Production implementation.
- N71 simplification direction approved: backup creation + restore are primary; rare legacy/bootstrap/inventory details use conditional/progressive disclosure. Safety-critical restore/owner semantics are not removed by this UX ticket.
- N73 is the Product feature ticket only: simplify and repair «تطبيق التوزيع على كل الفصول» so teachers can choose exact source items, see exact target status, avoid duplicate-origin traps, and never silently move student grades.

## D-094 — N36 direct official-source Helper/Extension direction — 2026-10-05
- Future N36 direction is a direct, user-initiated Madrasati/Noor Helper/Extension feeding the same N12 Preview and explicit confirmation. Official file-based exports remain N12 source adapters. PDF is only an optional fallback if a verified official format warrants it.
- Never request or store credentials or OTP and never run background surveillance. Candidate data may include teacher information, classes, rosters, schedule and grades only where genuinely accessible and verified for the source/session. Keep source provenance, owner isolation, privacy review and high-risk adapter/extension gates.
- This is direction for verified design and research; it does not approve a specific browser extension, collection method, private-data access, Product implementation or deployment.

## D-099 - N71 unified Cloud-first backup restore contract - 2026-10-06
- PO approved and froze the N71 V1 Product behavior: the normal user-facing page has one backup action and one restore action. Technical recovery topology is not presented as user choices.
- Backup remains one action: create/download a versioned backup file. The backup contract continues to exclude device/runtime-only stores such as device, meta, and outbox.
- Restore is one action: choose a backup file, validate it, show only the necessary safe review/confirmation, then execute the canonical account restore Cloud-first. After the cloud result is finalized, reconcile the current device to that canonical result and let ordinary Sync converge other verified devices.
- Normal users do not choose Local vs Cloud restore, Merge vs Replace, Curriculum Bootstrap, Legacy Workspace Claim, or Reconcile. Those are implementation/recovery mechanisms, not Product concepts.
- Do not implement this by using the current local restoreBackup() and assuming ordinary Sync will upload the restored snapshot. Current local restore writes IndexedDB through db.writeAll() without generating the versioned outbox intent needed to make that restored snapshot authoritative in the cloud.
- Reuse and extend the existing versioned Cloud Restore foundation rather than inventing a third restore system. Preserve owner checks, integrity/version validation, safe plan/review, conflict blocking, staged/finalized receipt semantics, resume-after-interruption, score/subitem invariants, lifecycle guards, and fail-closed behavior.
- The target restore scope is every user/Product data domain represented by the portable backup contract, with no silent omission. The backup file must contain all RAKEEZ user data needed to reconstruct Product state; only intentionally device/runtime-only state such as device, meta, outbox and ephemeral runtime receipts is excluded. Unified Cloud-first restore must apply every backed-up Product domain to the canonical account/cloud outcome, explicitly including curriculum units/lessons and any other Product stores present in the backup contract, including currently deferred domains such as assignments/submissions if they contain user data, then reconcile the current device to that exact canonical result so normal Sync converges other verified devices.
- device, meta, outbox, local runtime receipts and other intentionally device-scoped state remain excluded from portable backup/restore and are reconstructed/reconciled by the runtime.
- Legacy Workspace Claim is not a normal Settings feature. Keep it dormant/internal and surface it only for a proven legacy-workspace recovery state until a separate read-only retirement audit proves no supported user still needs it; only then may the mechanism be removed.
- Curriculum Bootstrap/Reconcile is not a normal Settings feature. Keep it internal only while required by the current units/lessons sync gate. Once the unified restore path safely owns curriculum restoration/provisioning, retire the separate user-facing/bootstrap recovery path if its gate can be removed without data or ownership risk.
- Signed-out, wrong-owner, offline, unhealthy-Sync, unresolved-outbox, or interrupted-restore states must fail closed or request the prerequisite needed by the same unified restore flow. Do not silently fall back to a divergent local-only restore that could later conflict with the account.
- The V1 page should remain simple: إنشاء نسخة احتياطية and استعادة نسخة احتياطية, plus only contextual status/error/recovery messaging when actually needed. No advanced-mode menu is required for the normal user.
- N71 remains HIGH-RISK for implementation because restore semantics, owner isolation, Sync convergence, curriculum data, deletion/tombstone handling, and interruption recovery are safety-critical. This decision approves Product behavior only; no migration, runtime, Supabase, schema, live data, Preview, or Production action is authorized by this docs record.

## D-107 - N44 notification foundation and secure admin publisher - 2026-10-06
- PO approves a complete reusable notification foundation rather than a deliberately crippled first version. Complete foundation does not mean every notification uses every channel; each notification type has its own appropriate channel rules.
- User-facing foundation includes an in-app notification bell/center with unread/read/dismiss semantics, expiry and deduplication; actionable notifications use deep links to the relevant RAKEEZ surface.
- Device delivery foundation includes real Web Push subscriptions per verified account/device. Pre-lesson reminders are considered useful only when they can reach the teacher through OS/device notification delivery while RAKEEZ is not open; an in-app-only reminder is insufficient.
- Support scheduling and multi-device delivery. Notification generation/delivery must be idempotent and must avoid duplicate/noisy fan-out when the same logical event is processed more than once.
- Retain the four product categories: operational teacher; account/service; RAKEEZ announcements; marketing/subscription offers. Category/channel preferences are separate where applicable. Marketing/offers are optional/opt-in. Critical account, security, ownership, data-protection or action-required notices may be non-optional but must remain calm and narrowly scoped.
- Email is part of the available channel toolkit for message types that justify it; it is not a default duplicate channel for ordinary operational reminders.
- Add a separate internal **RAKEEZ Admin Publisher** surface for authorized operators. It is not shown in normal teacher navigation and is not secured merely by hiding a route.
- Admin Publisher capabilities: draft; preview; test-send to the operator; choose audience (all users, selected users, and an extensible future segment model); choose category and allowed channels; title/body; optional deep link/action; send now or schedule; expiry; cancel a not-yet-sent scheduled publication where safe; and inspect bounded delivery outcome/status.
- Publishing to all users is represented as one server-side publication/campaign. The client must not enumerate all users or hold service-role credentials; a server-authorized worker/fan-out resolves eligible recipients, preferences and registered devices.
- Admin authorization must be enforced server-side through an explicit privileged identity/allowlist/role contract. Current Product schema does not provide a general admin-role foundation, so implementation requires a separate HIGH-risk Auth/authorization architecture gate. Client-side visibility checks are never sufficient.
- Current `support-notification-worker` is specific to N34 support email delivery and is not the N44 admin publisher. Reuse shared operational patterns only where safe; do not overload that worker into a general broadcast authority.
- This decision freezes Product behavior/direction only. It authorizes no live schema/RLS/Auth/provider/service-role/Push credential change, no mass notification send, and no Production rollout before architecture, security, privacy, abuse/noise, cost and device compatibility gates.

## D-108 - RAKEEZ Admin general management platform - 2026-10-06
- PO approves **RAKEEZ Admin** as the single private administrative management platform for RAKEEZ rather than creating unrelated one-off admin pages for each capability.
- RAKEEZ Admin is separate from normal teacher navigation and Product UX. An admin route being hidden is not security; every privileged read/write/action must be server-authorized.
- Build the foundation once: explicit administrator identity/role or tightly controlled allowlist, server-enforced authorization, least-privilege module permissions, secure session/access checks, and an audit trail for sensitive administrative actions.
- High-impact operations should support review/confirmation and, where appropriate, draft/preview/publish, test mode, scheduling, rollback/cancel-before-apply or other domain-specific safeguards. The exact safeguard depends on the module.
- The platform is modular. **Notifications/N44 is the first approved module** and owns campaign composition/publishing UI while N44 retains notification semantics, recipient/channel rules, delivery, preferences, Web Push and fan-out behavior.
- Future RAKEEZ Admin modules may include: official Calendar catalog/publisher; subscriptions/plans/entitlements; users/accounts; Support operations; RAKEEZ announcements/content; feature/config controls; and other Product administration raised later by the PO.
- The PO's intent is broad administrative readiness, but this does **not** create blanket unrestricted mutation authority. RAKEEZ Admin must not become a generic raw-database editor, must never expose service-role credentials to the browser, and must not bypass Product invariants, RLS/Owner Guard, lifecycle, privacy or audit protections.
- Each module retains its own domain contract, authorization scope, validation, destructive-action safeguards and release gates. A module touching Auth, billing, RLS/schema, private user data, Sync/lifecycle or destructive operations remains HIGH/CRITICAL as applicable and requires its own explicit implementation authority.
- User/account administration should expose only the minimum data needed for the approved operation. Do not provide casual browsing of private teacher/student Product data merely because an administrator exists.
- The future official Calendar admin publisher, if pursued, belongs inside RAKEEZ Admin, but D-108 does not approve the Calendar catalog schema/source-monitoring/runtime itself; that remains separately scoped/deferred.
- Existing N34 `support-notification-worker` remains a support-email delivery worker, not a general admin backend. Shared infrastructure may be reused only after security review.
- This decision freezes Product/platform direction only. It authorizes no live admin account, Auth role, allowlist, schema/RLS, service-role exposure, billing integration, private-data access, mass notification, deployment or Production mutation.

## D-113 - N77 simplified delete vs immutable closed-term reports - 2026-10-07
- PO approved the simplest N77 path: Archive is not part of explicit Delete and no new Archive complexity is added for N77.
- Explicit Delete removes the selected live Teaching/Section scope and its current user-visible operational data under D-106. Shared students/data outside the deleted scope survive.
- Immutable closed_term_reports snapshots are a deliberate exception to physical destructive cascade. Do not split, rewrite, supersede or delete a mixed term snapshot merely because one Teaching/Section was explicitly deleted.
- Such snapshots may remain stored internally as historical technical truth. Their retained bytes do not mean the deleted Teaching/Section remains active Product data.
- Any Product surface, export, restore or convergence path that consumes a retained closed-term snapshot must suppress deleted Teaching/Section scope using durable deletion evidence and must never resurrect that scope.
- Minimal tombstones/receipts remain allowed for anti-resurrection, idempotency and safe retry.
- This refinement resolves the only N77 Product ambiguity found by the 2026-10-07 cascade audit. It supersedes the earlier requirement to physically remove every report-supporting row when that row is an immutable mixed closed-term snapshot.
- N77 remains CRITICAL because live lifecycle/Sync/data-loss semantics are involved. No live SQL/schema/data mutation is authorized until the exact high-risk gate is reached.

## D-114 - N77 online-only server-validated destructive delete - 2026-10-07
- PO approved the final N77 initiation rule: explicit destructive Delete is online-only and server-validated.
- A device must not perform any local destructive delete while offline or before trusted server validation succeeds.
- The Delete action remains understandable in the UI. If the device is offline or validation cannot complete, RAKEEZ leaves data unchanged and shows a calm message that deletion requires an internet connection, with retry after connectivity returns.
- On Delete, the server revalidates the authenticated owner/workspace and the current canonical Section/Teaching relationships before deriving scope. Multiple active Teachings means selected Teaching only; final/only Teaching means whole Section/class.
- Scope is derived from current server truth, not potentially stale local state. If server state changed and safe scope cannot be established, fail closed and require refresh/retry; never broaden a delete silently.
- Once validated, the destructive lifecycle command is atomic/fail-closed and cascades the approved live Product scope under D-106/D-113. Shared identities/data outside the validated scope survive.
- Offline/stale devices converge afterward through tombstones/receipts and must not resurrect deleted scope. Offline initiation and queued destructive Delete are explicitly out of scope for N77 V1.
- D-113 still applies: immutable mixed closed-term snapshots are not rewritten/split/deleted merely for Delete and remain internal historical artifacts suppressed for deleted scope.
- This resolves the remaining N77 Product ambiguity and authorizes isolated CRITICAL implementation/certification only. It does not authorize live schema/data mutation or Production promotion before the existing high-risk gates.

## D-119 - N73 simple full-distribution copy with safe optional extra-item removal - 2026-10-07
- PO APPROVED and FROZE N73 V2 Product contract in `N73_SIMPLIFIED_DISTRIBUTION_V2.md`. This supersedes the conflicting N73 V1/D-098 three-state no-update/no-delete behavior; D-102 N01 regression obligations and D-105 parent edit safety remain. Previous N73 Work V2 is historical and NOT an implementation candidate for the copy workflow.
- Simplify the regular teacher flow to source class → select target classes → compact review → apply. Copy the whole distribution definition; update matching target items in place, create missing, avoid duplicates. Do not expose internal matching states/provenance or separate bulk modes.
- Target-only recorded manual score values stay where valid. On maximum reduction, values above new maximum are clamped in persisted score records (23/25→20/20), not display-only. Manual/auto changes use the target's own logs and never copy scores from source. Subitem/completion and owner/Sync correctness are HIGH-risk gates.
- Extra target items and their scores **remain untouched by default**. Under collapsed `عرض الأثر`, an unchecked checkbox `إزالة هذا البند` for each extra item allows explicit deletion after warning/confirmation. Keeping extras means full identity is not exact; this is accepted Product behavior.
- Truly ambiguous duplicate names/origin matches fail closed for the affected target with a clear explanation and a direct link to fix that target's items. No guesses or accidental deletion.
- Compact RTL mobile treatment and one parent `تحرير` + one `البنود الفرعية` action. No clutter or unnecessary review steps. Work is authorized to produce real-UI V3 candidate; Codex may start isolated pure planning/invariants and safe implementation lanes now. Preview/Production/high-risk live mutation and CLOSED remain subject to separate gates.

### D-119 implementation clarification (same PO approval, not a separate decision) - 2026-10-07
- Current PO approval: N73 new simpler contract is APPROVED FOR IMPLEMENTATION. It supersedes the D-098 three-state/no-update contract and the old Work N73 V2 candidate; preserve D-102/N01 idempotency regression and D-105 natural class order and metadata-only parent rename.
- Teacher chooses one reference class and one or more eligible target classes. No target is selected by default. Apply its parent distribution items, complete subitems, maximums and automatic/manual configuration. Target student grades/events are NEVER copied from the source class.
- A uniquely and safely matched existing target item is reconciled to the reference definition. Preserve target students' scores/completions where compatible; never erase scores merely to simplify matching. If a score exceeds the new maximum, cap at the new maximum (e.g. 23/25 -> 20/20), showing the effect before final confirmation. Other in-range numeric scores remain unchanged.
- If an existing manual item becomes automatic, show the data-effect warning and derive the new score exclusively from that target class's own matching Quick Log/other authoritative records, not the source class or an invented value. No direct auto-score overwrite outside the existing scoring projection contract.
- Reference items missing in the target are created without source students' grades; target automatic items derive only from target-side events. Repeated applications must be idempotent: no duplicate parent/subitem/origin creation.
- Extra target items absent from the reference are KEPT with all existing target student grades by default. Display: «نشاط صفي — غير موجود في رابع 1»; «سيبقى هذا البند ودرجات طلابه كما هي.»; unchecked option «إزالة هذا البند». Unchecked is the default, including reentry into the flow. Deletion is an explicit teacher choice, not a side effect of synchronization.
- If teacher selects removal, show the affected item's student-grade impact in the final review and require a distinct deliberate confirmation before any destructive commit. Never silently discard grades, and never transform an implicit unchecked state into consent.
- Preview is concise: reference, targets, total before/after, changes affecting grade interpretation; «عرض الأثر» initially collapsed. Avoid the old three-state technical workflow. Warnings appear only when an actual significant change requires attention.
- If multiple same-named target items or ambiguous identity/origin prevent a safe match, stop the ambiguous portion and direct the teacher to resolve the duplicate in target item settings. Do not guess a match, automatically create a duplicate, or quietly overwrite a different item.
- Parent rename remains available with/without subitems, metadata-only, preserving parent/subitem IDs, order, completions, scores and Sync lineage. Targets use natural class order. N01 duplicate-origin regression remains covered within N73, not a new lane.
- Codex owns actual high-risk score/source-match/atomic update/delete/Sync implementation; Work-Active owns only the integrated real RAKEEZ UI, not a standalone mock. No N73 Product/live mutation, SQL/Supabase write or Production promotion is authorized without its own gates.
- Lean execution rule: smallest isolated N73 slice, existing primitives first, tests proportional to risk. Prefer focused score-cap, manual-to-auto, explicit-extra-delete/keep, idempotency, failure/retry and owner isolation gates; reuse proven unchanged evidence and avoid broad duplicate suites, speculative framework work, and feature inflation.
- N73 HOLD is removed for this D-119 contract only. All old N73 Work candidates remain historical; any new N73 Work lane must not edit approved frozen W1/N82/N70/N84/N71 surfaces.

## D-120 - N77 explicit high-risk completion authorization - 2026-10-08
- PO explicitly authorized PM to undertake all steps necessary to deliver and finish N77, including the previously held live Supabase migration and bounded synthetic live verification, provided the already-approved D-104/D-106/D-113/D-114 deletion/owner/Sync/data-loss safeguards pass. This decision does not change N77 Product behavior.
- Live Supabase target is the verified production project RakeezX Main (xlrubcwjqktzzunrvuns). Read-only checks on 2026-10-08 confirmed the old lifecycle RPC exists and N77 migration/function/guard do not yet exist.
- Authorize applying only the exact reviewed additive N77 server-validated delete migration when a current-main N77 client candidate, exact SQL hash/schema checks, disposable native Postgres owner A/B/atomicity tests, client receipts/anti-resurrection and scoped recovery plan are certified. Applied migrations remain immutable. Stop on unexpected drift, unsafe compatibility, failed security/Sync tests, or live test mutation outside named disposable synthetic records. No raw Product/private account data mutations are authorized.
- Authorized live test operations are limited to identified disposable synthetic account A/B IDs and purpose-created classes, Teachings, students and descendants, with before/after checks and safe disposition. No unrelated schema/Auth/ownership/restore changes.
- Final Cloudflare Preview PO review, exact Production promotion, PO Production verification and CLOSED evidence remain mandatory for user-visible N77. This is not an authorization to skip HIGH/CRITICAL gates.
